clue.text: Former prisoner has to do it?

definitions.meaning: an adjective meaning one-time or erstwhile
a convict must serve a stretch inside

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what an ex-convict was obliged to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former prisoner' reads as an ex-con, but 'Former' is a definition on its own and the rest is a second definition split as SOME TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime as an adjective means former or one-time, a slightly literary usage.

clue.text: Wasps, perhaps, stick round a minor route

parts.note: Wasps is an English rugby union club, an example of a side or team

indicators.note: the rod goes round, enclosing the letter a

parts.note: a rod is a stick or pole

explanation.surface: Insects clinging around a quiet lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasps' looks like insects; it is a rugby club, hence a team or SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A side road is a minor street branching off a main one.

clue.text: Poorly interpret short film on court official

indicators.note: short means the word for film loses its final letter

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or haze, a mist
a judge presides in a law court

explanation.surface: Reading a brief movie about a judge the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' is not a movie here but a thin haze, MIST, cut to MIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To misjudge is to assess or read a situation wrongly.

clue.text: Grubby part of basement I redecorated

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A dingy section of a basement I have done up.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired describes things worn and shabby from use, which is close to grubby.

clue.text: Independent trader to get on back of dour administrative type

parts.note: a middleman is a trader between producer and buyer, working for himself
to get on in years is to age

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A self-employed trader taking on a gloomy bureaucrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A middle manager is an executive between senior and junior staff, often seen as an administrator.

clue.text: Outcome of lob in tennis?

definitions.meaning: a lob is a stroke hit high, so jokingly a shot that goes up

explanation.surface: Wondering what results from lobbing the ball at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful split into UP SHOT for the tennis stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot of something is its final result or consequence.

clue.text: It's hung oddly amid ceremonial splendour in French hotel in capital

indicators.note: amid says the picked letters sit in the middle of the word for splendour

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial show and splendour

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word

parts.note: en is French for in
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something hangs strangely amid grandeur in a French hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes H and N from 'hung', and 'amid' puts them inside POMP after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Phnom Penh is the capital city of Cambodia.

clue.text: Ring is seen on the wings of one bird

parts.note: a hoop is a ring or circular band

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outside letters

explanation.surface: A ring spotted on the wings of a single bird, as if ringed.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with a striking black-and-white barred wing.

clue.text: Versailles was noted for this feast before start of year

parts.note: a treat is a delightful indulgence, a feast

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The palace of Versailles was famous for lavish banquets.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the palace's banquets; the definition means the 1919 peace settlement signed there.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treaty of Versailles ended the First World War, the most famous accord signed at that palace.

clue.text: Ill-repute is harboured by Washington Republican? Correct

indicators.note: something harboured by another is sheltered within it, so the word is goes inside the next piece

parts.note: DC, the District of Columbia, is the US capital
to correct a text is to edit it

explanation.surface: Suggesting that a Republican in Washington is rightly held in poor regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Discredit as a noun means loss of reputation, the same as disrepute.

clue.text: Note floor rotting around Western fellow in fortified landmark

indicators.note: around means the rotten letters are placed on either side of the single letter for Western
rotting suggests decay and breaking up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a don is a fellow or tutor of an Oxford or Cambridge college

explanation.surface: A decaying floor around a western man in an old fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotting' rearranges NOTE FLOOR as TO-EROFLON, and 'around' places it about W before DON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tower of London is a Norman fortress beside the Thames, a famous historic site.

clue.text: Snare readily recalled close to hedge

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for readily runs backwards

parts.note: soon can mean readily or willingly, as in 'I'd as soon go'

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so take the final letter of hedge

explanation.surface: A trap easily remembered as lying by a hedgerow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'readily' gives SOON in its old sense of willingly, as in 'I would sooner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a looped cord used as a snare for catching animals.

clue.text: Chicago visitor might go so for a disc

parts.note: a visitor might go round, that is drop in or circle the city's Loop
the El (or L) is Chicago's elevated railway

explanation.surface: A tourist in Chicago perhaps going a certain way for a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a direction: a visitor goes round the El, Chicago's elevated railway, whose Loop circles downtown.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundel is a small circular disc or emblem, such as the RAF marking on aircraft.

clue.text: Caribbean maiden with sulky expression gets to lose nerve

parts.note: WI stands for the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over
a pout is a sulky pushing out of the lips

explanation.surface: A sulking woman from the Caribbean ends up losing her courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To wimp out is an informal idiom for backing down through fear.

clue.text: Article with line about Greek meal prepared for powerful politician

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit about, that is around, the single letter for line
a meal prepared is made up from its ingredients, so the letters of Greek meal are reworked

explanation.surface: A Greek dinner cooked up for a mighty leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges GREEK MEAL into GE-AMERKEL, and 'about' wraps those letters around L after GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela Merkel was German Chancellor for sixteen years, widely called Europe's most powerful leader.

clue.text: Label a hug that's contrived as ridiculous

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Calling a forced embrace absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laughable is so absurd that it invites mockery.

clue.text: Dancer with partner snubbed by a women's quarters barring male

indicators.note: snubbed is read as cut short, as a snub nose is, so the word loses its tail

parts.note: a mate is a partner

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so the letter for male is removed

parts.note: harim is a variant spelling of harem, the women's part of a household

explanation.surface: A dancer cold-shouldered by her partner in a harem with no men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubbed' cuts MATE to MAT; HARIM is a variant of harem.
explanation.definitionFit: Mata Hari was a Dutch exotic dancer executed as a spy in 1917.

clue.text: Small amount of money put in bank not long ago

indicators.note: put in signals one piece placed inside the other

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a small coin, a hundredth of a dollar

explanation.surface: Depositing a few coins at the bank lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like the place money goes; it is the verb, as in 'bank on', RELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, at a time shortly before now.

clue.text: Fear short pun is flawed as evidence of linguistic ability

indicators.note: flawed suggests the words are broken and must be reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Worrying that a brief joke is weak proof of someone's verbal skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like an instruction to cut 'Fear', but it is simply part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat turn of phrase is a deft expression, showing skill with words.

clue.text: Get in boat at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Climbing aboard a vessel on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to get or acquire it.

clue.text: Limit to endurance over work producing strike

parts.note: runners 'hit the wall' at the limit of their stamina
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A worker reaching breaking point and going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; it means a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallop is a hard thump or blow.

clue.text: Listen to security device after exchanging leads in hold

indicators.note: leads are first letters, so the opening letters of the two words swap places

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
a bug is a hidden listening device used in surveillance

explanation.surface: Eavesdropping on a wiretap after swapping cables while held.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear hug is a tight, rough embrace, a kind of hold in wrestling.

clue.text: Disclosed revenue in part of film not broadcast

parts.note: out means revealed, as a secret is out
the take is the money taken in, the takings

explanation.surface: Box-office income revealed in an unseen scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An outtake is footage cut from the final edit, often shown later as a blooper.

clue.text: One, say, familiar with testing scales in fish, it's said

definitions.text: One, say, familiar with testing scales

indicators.note: it's said signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: the tuna is a large sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone who checks the scales of a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' suggests fish scales; it is musical scales, tested by a piano tuner. The homophone works in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A piano tuner plays scales to check and adjust the instrument's pitch.

clue.text: Expression that's improvised in a German paper on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows a mirror image, so the name of the paper is read backwards

parts.note: Bild is Germany's best-selling tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A spontaneous remark in a German newspaper, thought over afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad-lib is a remark made up on the spot rather than scripted.

clue.text: Unusually rude worker covering new department no longer employed

indicators.note: covering means the outer pieces wrap over the two short abbreviations
unusually signals the letters of rude in a strange order

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A rude worker taking over a fresh department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' scrambles only 'rude'; 'covering' then has the scrambled word plus the worker wrap the two single-letter abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone made redundant has lost their job because the post is no longer needed.

clue.text: Mobile say not working kept by strange relative

indicators.note: something kept by another is held within it, so the shortened gadget sits inside

parts.note: new can mean unfamiliar or strange, as in 'this place is new to me'

indicators.note: on means working or operating, so those two letters are dropped

parts.note: a mobile is an example of a phone

explanation.surface: An odd family member holding a broken mobile phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' removes ON from PHONE to leave PHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is a sibling's son, a family relation.

clue.text: Offence that's major or minor type possibly when quietly ignored

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters could form another word when rearranged
ignored means left out, so the letter for quietly is dropped

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Debating whether a misdeed is serious or trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when quietly ignored' drops P from MINOR TYPE, and 'possibly' rearranges the remaining MINORTYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormity in its strict sense means a grave crime or outrageous wickedness.
